reasoning: The question asks whether there will be no change in Fed interest rates after the April 2026 meeting (April 28-29). Based on the evidence: (1) The Fed held rates unchanged in January 2026 at 3.50-3.75%, continuing a pause after three 2025 cuts. (2) Most economists forecast only two rate cuts in 2026, likely in June or later, not April. (3) Fed officials emphasize caution near neutral rates and stress that cuts would only come if inflation declines substantially. (4) As of early March 2026, there's no indication of imminent April rate changes. (5) The Fed faces divided opinions but the consensus leans toward maintaining current rates through spring 2026. Given that most forecasts point to rate cuts beginning in June at earliest, and the Fed's cautious stance near neutral rates, a no-change outcome in April appears likely.
